page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical Intel Xeon 8369B cores operating at a speed of 2.7 GHz. The processor includes a 48 MB L3 cache and supports instruction set extensions such as AVX-512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AES cryptography. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.r7.2xlarge delivers mid-tier performance across most standardized tests. Its single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls within the average range (middle 50%). Memory bandwidth tests, including read and write operations on large uncached blocks, also place the instance in the middle 50% tier. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25%. Additionally, while the instance handles small-model LLM inference (135M) with average efficiency, its performance drops to the bottom 10% for medium-model (7B) LLM inference, highlighting a clear limitation for complex machine learning tasks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r7.2xlarge offers a high density of memory relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-performance local storage or GPU acceleration. The instance is suited for database operations, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and general-purpose memory-intensive applications. It is less suitable for compute-heavy parallel processing or large-scale language model inference due to its average CPU performance and poor multi-threaded decompression and medium-model LLM benchmarks.
